question: Where can I get a list of wind farms in operation in the United States, with location, capacity (MW), number of turbines, operator and commissioning date?

answer.summary: Two official US datasets together answer the question. The USGS U.S. Wind Turbine Database (v9.1, 28 Sep 2026) has a verified coordinate per turbine, project name, project-phase turbine count and MW, and commissioning year, via API and CSV. EIA-860 (final 2025 data) adds operator (the company running each generator), nameplate MW, turbine count and month/year per generator, at plant level. The two join on USWTDB eia_id = EIA Plant Code; the join is incomplete. USWTDB has no operator field.
main_caveats: USWTDB counts turbines (77,839 records, 129 offshore); EIA-860 counts generator records (1,573 operable wind) in plants. Aggregate to project/plant before comparing.
USWTDB eia_id is null for 5,051 turbine records, and 95 of 1,371 EIA wind plants have no turbine in USWTDB, so the join is partial.
USWTDB offshore turbines are mostly state 'NA' and often lack eia_id; USWTDB p_tnum/p_cap describe a phase, not always the whole farm.
USWTDB locations are visually checked, not field-verified (~10 m tolerance); EIA gives one plant point, not turbine positions.
EIA-860 is annual (latest final = 2025 data); EIA-860M monthly adds status/coordinates but no turbine count or owner shares.
answer.confidence_reason: Both official datasets were downloaded and queried on 2026-11-19; one farm (Roscoe, TX) was traced across both and the join rates were computed.

attributes.note: USWTDB: lon/lat per turbine, ~10 m tolerance; EIA-860 Plant sheet: one plant point (4-6 decimals).
USWTDB p_cap (MW, project phase) and t_cap (kW per turbine); EIA nameplate MW per generator.
USWTDB p_tnum per project phase and one row per turbine; EIA-860 Wind sheet 'Number of Turbines' per generator.
EIA 'Utility Name' = company responsible for day-to-day operation of each generator; ownership split in the Owner sheet.
attributes.gap_note: USWTDB has no operator/owner field and GEM no longer updates operators outside China. Operator is available only through the EIA join, for plants with a join.

attributes.note: EIA-860: Operating Month and Year per generator; USWTDB p_year = operational year per phase.

how_to_use.example_result: Roscoe, Nolan County TX: p_year 2008, p_tnum 209, p_cap 209.00 MW, one point -100.62370, 32.44849 (209 turbine rows for eia_id 56593).
steps: Page with Range/Prefer: count=exact headers or set limit=100000 (full pull of 16.5 MB JSON succeeded).
Group by eia_id (or p_name+t_state+p_year) to get projects.
Join eia_id to EIA-860 'Plant Code' for operator and generator data.
reading_traps: One row is a turbine, not a farm.
p_tnum/p_cap describe a phase (125 eia_ids have more than one p_year).
API example in the docs shows p_tnum 1 / p_cap 1.6 for case 3038257, but the live record returns 6 / 9.60: the docs sample is outdated.

history.note: Downloaded EIA-860 2025 and EIA-860M Sep 2026, USWTDB v9.1 via API and CSV, traced Roscoe (TX) and Block Island (RI), computed join rates. Effort level not exposed to the model; the user launched it as Sonnet High. Counts are estimates.

local_terms.meaning: USWTDB 'project' (p_name) and EIA 'plant' (Plant Code) are the farm-level units; a plant can hold several generator records.
